S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours for incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or emergency-service response, and within 10 business days for other confirmed thermal incidents.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model exceeds the acceptance criterion if more than 5% of tested units fail. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sales; the regulator may impose proportionate interim measures based on demonstrated risk while corrective actions are underway. Before purchase, current and prospective customers must receive the model's current test status and its complete per-model test results, including the measured failure rate; these results must also be available to existing customers.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of safe operation. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit pathway for installed units that are technically compatible, completing required retrofits within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where retrofitting is infeasible, the manufacturer must notify the owner and provide safe alternative mitigation.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard is adopted. The system must be designed and validated to applicable regulator-approved performance and maintenance requirements.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator, investigate the causes, and submit a corrective-action plan. The manufacturer must initiate a recall for that model, promptly contact affected customers, provide a remedy, and give safe-use instructions.

document.section_notes: The final v17 S2 lets a model above 5% keep selling, with only discretionary regulator interim measures, which mainly protects Northwind's Hearth 10 at 6.2%. S5 makes recall mandatory at 8 per 100,000 with no transition, which hits Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9, while customers get numeric per-model results without public publication. S1 and S3 sit within the acceptable ranges, and S4 meets Halcyon's 36-month floor.
